She cast away her initial fears and stepped onto the stage.
They were cast away on an isolated island following the shipwreck.

meaning: Aprovecharse de / Sacar ventaja indebida de alguien
examples: Naive people are easily taken advantage of because they assume universal benevolence.

meaning: Retroceder / Dar un paso atrás ante la firmeza
examples: A clear show of strength and composure often makes a bully back off immediately.

When she stood her ground, the aggressive customer backed off.
The aggressive predator backed off into the dark tree line.

meaning: Disparar indiscriminadamente / Subir o dispararse con rapidez
examples: Weak, resentful men are often the ones who shoot up schools.

Interest rates began to shoot up unexpectedly during the financial crisis.
Crime rates shoot up in neighborhoods that lack social cohesion.
The young athlete shot up six inches in height over a single summer.

meaning: Pasar a un segundo plano / Relegarse voluntariamente
examples: Young men are often wrongfully encouraged to take a back seat in competitive environments.

Her creative ambitions took a back seat while she raised three infants.
Never take a back seat when your fundamental rights are being negotiated.
In times of national emergency, political disputes must take a back seat.

meaning: Clamar por / Exigir o necesitar desesperadamente
examples: Part of the psyche cries out for the incorporation of the inner monster.

Vulnerable communities are crying out for genuine moral leadership.
Her pale and exhausted face cried out for rest and proper nutrition.
The historical injustices in that nation cry out for judicial reckoning.

meaning: Disiparse con el viento / Desvanecerse ante el primer embate
examples: Impulsive pleasure blows away at the first ill wind of tragedy.
All their grand theoretical plans blew away when real conflict erupted.
Superficial alliances blow away the second financial pressure mounts.
His fleeting arrogance blew away when he confronted the harsh wilderness.
Dry autumn leaves blow away under the fury of November gales.

meaning: Recaer / Abandonar una disciplina o sobriedad
examples: If your schedule is purely tyrannical, you will fall off the wagon within three days.

Strict unrealistic diets cause many people to fall off the wagon quickly.

meaning: Fijar el blanco / Concentrarse intensamente en una meta
examples: Dopamine helps your attention lock on to a meaningful, difficult pursuit.
The heat-seeking missile locked on to the exhaust signature.
Her eyes locked on to the subtle error in the financial ledger.
When inspired by noble purpose, the human mind locks on with remarkable stamina.
He locked on to the chess board, completely oblivious to room noise.

meaning: Incrementar / Potenciar / Activar una respuesta biológica
examples: Stimulant medications tap up the dopamine response to foster focus.
Rigorous physical training taps up your body's cardiovascular endurance.
The team tapped up their operational efforts to meet the strict deadline.
Good nutrition can tap up your cognitive sharpness during grueling exams.
Inspirational music taps up emotional engagement in theatrical narratives.

meaning: Idear / Evocar / Producir ingeniosamente de la nada
examples: The brain works tirelessly to conjure up a viable solution to the crisis.

Smelling old cedar wood conjured up vivid childhood memories of his grandfather.
They had to conjure up sufficient emergency funds before the bank closed.
A great novelist conjures up complex worlds from raw human observation.

meaning: Relevar a alguien del cansancio / Dar un respiro en una tarea
examples: You must step in and spell off your exhausted partner when taking care of an infant.

Nurses take turns to spell each other off during grueling twelve-hour shifts.
He offered to drive and spell off his father on the long highway trek.

meaning: Fragmentar / Dividir mentalmente en partes manejables
examples: Your perceptual system chops up reality into functional tools and obstacles.
He chopped up the monumental writing project into daily three-hundred-word goals.
Don't try to solve the crisis all at once; chop it up into tactical stages.
The executive chopped up the failing department into specialized divisions.
She chopped up the raw logs to feed the wood stove for the winter.

meaning: Arrastrar / Dejarse engullir por un engaño o situación turbia
examples: How did I get sucked into a dysfunctional relationship with someone I didn't truly know?
He warned his daughter not to get sucked into campus political drama.
Thousands of naive investors were sucked into the fraudulent pyramid scheme.
She was sucked into a destructive cycle of online arguments and anxiety.
Small nations often get sucked into the geopolitical conflicts of superpowers.

meaning: Derrocar / Desmoronar una estructura opresiva
examples: Solzhenitsyn's literary testimony helped bring down the totalitarian Soviet apparatus.
A monumental financial scandal brought down the prime minister's government.
Persistent individual integrity can bring down deeply corrupt institutional hierarchies.
Severe drought brought down several ancient Mediterranean civilizations.
The public revelations brought down the corrupt corporate board within weeks.

meaning: Agazaparse / Encogerse con cautela
examples: The cautious rat hunched down and scanned the unfamiliar room before advancing.
He hunched down behind the low stone wall to evade sniper fire.
The frightened child hunched down in the closet until the shouting stopped.
Sailors hunched down on the deck as massive waves broke over the bow.
Hunching down against the freezing blizzard kept them from fatal hypothermia.

meaning: Desviar / Mover de un lado a otro como un estorbo
examples: The neglected orphan was shunted from foster home to foster home for years.
Bureaucrats kept shunting his urgent application from one office to another.
Patients were constantly shunted between clinics without receiving a diagnosis.
He felt dehumanized being shunted from department to department in the corporation.
Trains were shunted from the main track to allow the express locomotive to pass.

meaning: Abarrotar / Llenar de desorden caótico
examples: Unaddressed domestic issues clutter up the mind and breed chronic anxiety.
Trivial possessions cluttered up the garage until nobody could walk inside.
Don't clutter up your life goals with superficial status symbols.
Excessive bureaucratic paperwork clutters up clinical therapeutic practice.
Irrelevant data points cluttered up the scientific report and obscured the truth.

meaning: Depurar / Eliminar lo defectuoso o inútil
examples: You must continually weed out self-deceptive habits from your daily conduct.
The rigorous selection process was designed to weed out undisciplined recruits.
Editors work tirelessly to weed out redundant sentences from scholarly manuscripts.
Weed out the toxic acquaintances who secretly celebrate your missteps.
A healthy organization routinely weeds out corrupt practices before they take root.

meaning: Desviarse súbitamente / Salirse de la ruta correcta
examples: Jonah veered off the ethical pathway commanded by the divine voice.
The vehicle veered off the slick highway into the snowy ditch.

His career veered off track following the devastating public scandal.
The ship veered off course to avoid underwater coral shoals.

meaning: Expulsar / Escupir hacia fuera
examples: After days in the dark belly of the whale, Jonah was spit up on the dry shore.
The infant spit up milk on his father's freshly pressed shirt.
The rough surf spit up pieces of old wreckage upon the pebbled beach.
The machine malfunctioned and spit up shredded documents onto the warehouse floor.
The turbulent ocean spit up the exhausted swimmer onto the rocky reef.

meaning: Degenerar en espiral / Caer en picado hacia la ruina
examples: Everyone knows where they would end up if they let their worst habits augur down.

The negotiations augured down into sterile acrimony and mutual accusations.

meaning: Arruinar / Destruir / Agotar por completo
examples: Staying in a soul-crushing job out of cowardice will ultimately do you in.

Chronic domestic resentment will do your romantic relationship in over time.
A sudden legal lawsuit did the small manufacturing business in.
Unchecked greed and hubris did the ancient empire in.

meaning: Conformarse con / Aceptar algo inferior a regañadientes
examples: Do not settle for shallow hedonism when profound meaning is within your reach.

Too many people settle for comfort because confronting adventure terrifies them.
He was determined never to settle for superficial, sycophantic friendships.

meaning: Chocar frontalmente / Enfrentarse tercamente
examples: Immature partners constantly butt heads instead of pursuing constructive dialogue.

Stop butting heads with the referee; accept the ruling and play on.
Father and son butted heads for decades before reaching mutual forgiveness.
Rival political factions butted heads incessantly, paralyzing legislative progress.

meaning: Irradiar potencial destructivo / Transmitir una amenaza implícita pero controlada
examples: A disciplined martial artist radiates potential for havoc without ever throwing a blow.

A formidable sovereign must radiate potential for havoc to preserve regional peace.
Beneath his impeccable etiquette, you could sense a man who radiated potential for havoc.

meaning: Dieta de papilla intelectual / Discurso simplón, blando y edulcorado
examples: Modern society has been fed a diet of pablum rights devoid of ethical duties.
Students rebelled against the patronizing curriculum, rejecting its diet of pablum.
Instead of real historical analysis, television viewers are served a sterile diet of pablum.
He refused to consume the political party's diet of sentimental pablum.
Adult minds deteriorate when nourished solely on a cultural diet of pablum.

meaning: Parte integrante / Elemento inseparable de un todo
examples: Voluntary responsibility and true personal meaning are part and parcel of the same reality.

Rigorous self-scrutiny is part and parcel of becoming a competent clinician.
Making mistakes is part and parcel of acquiring high-level mastery.

meaning: Sermonear con superioridad moral / Dar lecciones con paternalismo
examples: People listen to authentic mentors who include themselves rather than finger waving from above.

His lecture was ineffective because it felt like condescending finger waving from above.
A good parent leads by embodied example rather than arbitrary finger waving from above.
Stop finger waving from above and get your hands dirty in the actual work.

word: The meek shall inherit the Earth
meaning: Los mansos heredarán la tierra (aquellos con espada que la mantienen envainada)
examples: The biblical phrase 'the meek shall inherit the earth' truly refers to disciplined power, not harmlessness.

In Peterson's analysis, 'the meek shall inherit the earth' is an injunction for armed, restrained virtue.

meaning: Desarrollar agallas / Hacerse temible / Aprender a defenderse
examples: It is impossible to respect yourself until you grow teeth and establish boundaries.
The gentle teacher had to grow teeth to manage the unruly classroom.
When dealing with aggressive corporate rivals, you better grow teeth quickly.
She finally grew teeth and refused to accept unfair working terms.

meaning: Nada fácil / Un camino duro y desagradable
examples: Confronting your own capacity for historical atrocities is no picnic.

Medical school rotations in trauma surgery are certainly no picnic.
Facing clinical depression without therapeutic support is no picnic.
Rebuilding a broken marriage after an affair is definitely no picnic.

word: Separate the wheat from the chaff
meaning: Separar el trigo de la paja / Distinguir lo valioso de lo inservible
examples: Honest self-criticism enables you to separate the wheat from the chaff in your personality.

Editors must separate the wheat from the chaff before sending the draft to print.
Historical crises separate the wheat of true leaders from the chaff of mere orators.

meaning: Acelerador a fondo / Al límite absoluto de revoluciones
examples: When involuntary panic kicks in, your physiology pushes the pedal to the metal.

word: At the drop of a hat
meaning: A la mínima / Al instante y sin dudarlo
examples: You can decide to clean and organize your bedroom at the drop of a hat.

A disciplined soldier is ready for tactical deployment at the drop of a hat.

meaning: Cortar las piernas / Dejar incapacitado ante un golpe fatal del destino
examples: Tragic medical emergencies can cut an energetic individual off at the knees.

A catastrophic injury cut the promising athlete's career off at the knees.
Life's arbitrary tragedies sometimes cut good people off at the knees without warning.

meaning: Tocar una fibra sensible / Resonar profundamente
examples: Ancient mythological narratives strike a deep chord within the human soul.
Her impassioned speech about human freedom struck a deep chord with the young crowd.
The poignant musical piece struck a deep chord in everyone attending the memorial.
A profound psychological insight strikes a deep chord of intuitive remembering.
His personal struggles with grief struck an immediate deep chord among his listeners.

meaning: Hasta los topes / Abarrotado por completo
examples: The dysfunctional household was packed to the rafters with studiously ignored resentments.
The historic concert hall was crammed to the rafters for the symphony premiere.
His mind felt jammed to the rafters with unresolved professional anxieties.
The ancient barn was filled to the rafters with sweet-smelling dry hay.

meaning: Desde el primer momento / De entrada
examples: You can tell right off the bat whether a speaker understands human nature.

meaning: En bandeja de plata / Sin esfuerzo alguno
examples: If everything is handed to you on a silver platter, you are deprived of self-respect.

meaning: Desgarrarse por las costuras / Desmoronarse internamente

meaning: Transmutar / Transformar algo oscuro en una fuerza superior
examples: The goal of psychological maturity is to transmute destructive impulses into disciplined strength.

meaning: Envainar / Contener un arma o impulso agresivo

meaning: Regañar duramente / Reprender con severidad

meaning: Acumularse con el tiempo / Devengar consecuencias
examples: The penalty for avoiding adult maturity accrues silently until it suddenly crushes you.

Remarkable physical endurance accrues through small, daily, disciplined exertions.

meaning: Mitigar / Aliviar / Mejorar una condición precaria

meaning: Agente estresante / Factor provocador de estrés

meaning: Bálsamo / Alivio o consuelo reconfortante

meaning: Hombre de paja / Falacia de caricaturizar el argumento ajeno
examples: Do not construct a trivial straw man of your spouse's argument just to win a domestic spat.

meaning: Guarida / Madriguera de una bestia temible

A lack of liquid capital hindered the promising biotech startup from scaling production.

meaning: Impedir / Obstruir físicamente o frenar el avance
examples: Massive fallen rockslides impeded traffic along the primary Alpine highway.
Inadequate funding directly impedes the hospital's capacity to purchase medical scanners.
Do not allow minor logistical hiccups to impede the overarching project timeline.
Hostile naval blockades impeded the delivery of essential food and fuel shipments.
Structural corruption impedes equitable economic distribution throughout the commonwealth.

meaning: Instigar / Incitar o provocar una rebelión, disputa o investigación
examples: Radical agitators attempted to instigate a general transport strike across the city.
The regulatory agency decided to instigate a formal inquiry into anti-competitive pricing.
He was accused of instigating the violent altercation in the hotel lobby.
Progressive civic groups instigated an independent review of local municipal zoning.
Rumors circulating online instigated widespread panic and bank runs.

meaning: Atenuar / Mitigar la gravedad, impacto o crudeza de algo
examples: Planting native mangrove forests along coastlines helps mitigate storm surge damage.
Early therapeutic intervention can mitigate the long-term cognitive impact of trauma.
The corporate committee adopted strict fiscal protocols to mitigate financial risk.
Painkillers and physical rehabilitation helped mitigate his chronic postoperative discomfort.
Transitioning to electric transport is essential to mitigate metropolitan air pollution.

meaning: Ocultar / Ensombrecer o hacer confusa una verdad evidente
examples: Thick industrial smog obscured the scenic mountain backdrop of the capital.
Unnecessary technical jargon only serves to obscure the fundamental message of the paper.
The politician deliberately tried to obscure the financial ties between his donors and the bill.
Do not allow minor procedural squabbles to obscure our shared strategic destination.
Clouds gathered quickly and obscured the full moon just before midnight.

meaning: Perpetuar / Hacer que algo (generalmente malo o falso) se prolongue indefinidamente
examples: Sensationalist media coverage often perpetuates harmful ethnic stereotypes.
Failing to enforce standard penalties perpetuates a culture of corporate corruption.
Sycophantic advisors merely perpetuate the tyrant's dangerous delusions.
Outdated educational curricula perpetuate socio-economic inequality across generations.
Do not perpetuate malicious office rumors that you cannot verify independently.

meaning: Postular / Proponer como premisa o hipótesis para el debate
examples: Theoretical cosmologists postulate the existence of higher spatial dimensions.
The macroeconomic model postulates that consumer demand drives employment cycles.
Psychologists postulate that chronic stress degrades neurological neuroplasticity.
He postulated that the ancient civilization collapsed due to abrupt climatic shifts.
We must postulate certain foundational axioms before constructing our ethical framework.

meaning: Descartar / Imposibilitar de antemano que algo ocurra
examples: His severe spinal condition unfortunately precluded him from military aviation duty.
A prior non-disclosure agreement precluded the scientist from publishing the findings.
Signing this commercial exclusivity clause does not preclude future joint partnerships.
Poverty should never preclude promising youths from accessing tertiary education.
The heavy blizzard precluded any possibility of an emergency air evacuation.

meaning: Promulgar / Publicar y difundir solemnemente una ley o doctrina
examples: The monarch promulgated a revolutionary decree abolishing hereditary serfdom.
The regulatory agency promulgated updated safety guidelines for pharmaceutical manufacturing.
Enlightenment thinkers promulgated principles of natural rights and religious tolerance.
The new constitutional amendments will be officially promulgated on national independence day.
Religious leaders promulgated an urgent pastoral letter calling for regional reconciliation.

meaning: Refutar / Rebatir un argumento con pruebas fehacientes
examples: The defense attorney effectively rebutted every argument raised by the prosecution.
The research scientist published a comprehensive monograph to rebut her detractors' claims.
He took to the podium to rebut accusations of financial corruption and perjury.
Empirical economic data readily rebuts the simplistic assumptions of the manifesto.
She listened attentively before stepping up to rebut his assertions point by point.

meaning: Conciliar / Hacer compatibles dos posturas contrarias o perdonarse
examples: It is difficult to reconcile high corporate profits with widespread employee exploitation.
The estranged brothers met privately after twenty years to reconcile their differences.
Accountants worked overtime to reconcile discrepancies between invoices and bank ledgers.
How does one reconcile absolute deterministic physics with authentic human free will?
She struggled to reconcile her demanding career ambitions with domestic family duties.

meaning: Escrutar / Examinar con lupa y minucioso detalle
examples: Regulatory inspectors thoroughly scrutinized the factory's biochemical waste disposal logs.
Financial analysts scrutinized the company's balance sheet for hidden corporate liabilities.
The parliamentary committee scrutinized the proposed legislation line by line.
Her body language was scrutinized intensely by reporters during the press conference.
Scholars must scrutinize primary historical documents rather than relying on hearsay.

meaning: Sustanciar / Probar o fundamentar con datos verificables
examples: You cannot make bold public accusations without presenting concrete evidence to substantiate them.
Forensic pathology findings substantiated the detective's theory of foul play.
The claimant failed to produce documentation to substantiate his injury lawsuit.
Extensive geological samples substantiated the hypothesis of a prehistoric asteroid impact.
She submitted bank statements and signed receipts to substantiate her expense claims.

meaning: Subrayar / Poner de relieve la importancia crucial de algo
examples: The catastrophic blackout underscored our total vulnerability to electrical grid collapse.
The medical director underscored the imperative need for strict clinical hand hygiene.
Recent diplomatic tensions underscore the fragility of peaceful international treaties.
Her poignant testimony underscored the emotional toll borne by frontline nursing staff.
Statistical studies continually underscore the direct correlation between literacy and longevity.

meaning: Vindicar / Demostrar la inocencia o el acierto de alguien tras ser juzgado o dudado
examples: Fresh DNA testing finally vindicated the innocent prisoner after thirty years behind bars.
Subsequent economic expansion vindicated the central banker's controversial interest cuts.
His theoretical predictions were vindicated when astronomers photographed the black hole.
She felt fully vindicated when independent auditors confirmed her accounting warnings.
History frequently vindicates courageous dissidents whom contemporaries condemned.
